reason: E3 directly supports dynamic amorphization, ultra-nanocrystalline layer formation, and cavitation-induced nanoporosity in CoCrFeMnNi under high-strain-rate sliding in vacuum, but the cited evidence does not establish that this amorphization and cavitation cause brittle intergranular fracture or toughness degradation; E1 and E2 discuss impurity-driven precipitation and PFZ formation in a different alloy system and are misrepresented as supporting the absence of segregation effects.
premises: High strain-rate or elevated temperature loading induces extreme dynamic grain refinement in single-phase CCAs
Dynamic grain refinement leads to local amorphization of grain boundaries
Amorphization generates nanoporosity/cavitation along high-angle grain boundaries
Nanoporosity reduces grain boundary cohesive strength, causing intergranular decohesion
This mechanism operates without impurity segregation or intermetallic precipitation
